sources.entry: urwid - A library for creating terminal GUI applications with strong support for widgets, events, rich colors, etc.

summary.one_liner: Urwid is a Python console user interface library for building terminal GUI applications with widgets, event handling, and rich color support.
summary.what_it_does: Urwid provides a set of text-console UI building blocks for Python, including pre-built widgets such as edit boxes, buttons, check boxes and radio buttons. It offers automatic, programmable text alignment and wrapping, and simple markup for setting text attributes within blocks of text. A scrollable list box can hold programmable content of any widget type. It supports multiple display modules (raw, curses, and experimental LCD and web displays) and color modes including 24-bit true color, 256 color, and 88 color. Applications can plug into several event loops: Twisted, Glib (deprecated), Tornado, asyncio, trio, ZeroMQ, or a select-based loop.
use_cases: Building terminal user interfaces in Python
Creating interactive text-mode dashboards or forms
Adding widgets like buttons and edit boxes to console apps
Integrating a terminal UI with asyncio, Twisted, or trio event loops
Displaying colored, wrapped, or aligned text in a console
how_to_run: pip install urwid[serial,zmq]  # optional extras for ZeroMQ loop and LCD display
notable: Choice of event loops including asyncio, Twisted, Tornado, trio, and ZeroMQ
Pre-built widget set with a scrollable list box for any widget type
Color support up to 24-bit true color
Includes a Terminal widget (urwid.vterm) on supported platforms
Compatible with CPython 3.11+, free-threaded CPython, PyPy, and GraalPy (experimental)
caveats: Windows support is limited to Windows 10+; the Terminal widget, non-socket file descriptors, and ZMQEventLoop are not supported there
GLib event loop is deprecated; GLib and ZeroMQ are unsupported on free-threaded CPython and PyPy
GraalPy support is experimental and lacks curses and the Terminal widget
